eligibility.quote: I create two different Project on different workspace. One is idfa_msgs/GDXBoxesMessage under Rosjava 0.2.. The other is obstacle_detection/GDXBoxMessage under Roscpp.
eligibility.reason: The two independently built nodes attempt a PAIR connection on /box. The concrete connection log establishes E1/E4. Their nominal message declarations differ even though the topic name matches, so E2 is an interface failure rather than deployment-only wiring. E3 holds.

failed_conditions.quote: It looks like idfa_msgs/GDXBoxesMessage is not the same package (and thus message) as obstacle_detection/GDXBoxMessage.
failed_conditions.reason: The topic and both qualified message names are directly shown. The mismatch is nominal; equal field contents would not make those names identical.

loudness.quote: [ERROR] [1617170692.958476152]: Client [/GPUPlanarRegionSubscriber] wants topic /box to have datatype/md5sum [idfa_msgs/GDXBoxesMessage/d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e], but our version has [obstacle_detection/GDXBoxMessage/bbc122c887def5dd8eda16d81d7d1109]. Dropping connection.
loudness.reason: ROS explicitly rejects the connection and names both incompatible interfaces.

detection_stage.quote: However, when establishing the connection using customized message, the error pops up like following.
detection_stage.reason: The reporter and dropping-connection log both identify connect.

resolution.quote: Have java expect the lidar_obstacle_detection/gdxboxesmessage, have the c++ ros node use the java message, or create another node that subscribers to one and published the other. But I dont know how to do either of these
resolution.reason: The thread proposes aligning one side's message declaration with the other or introducing a translator. S1 explicitly includes proposed changes in recommended; absence of an implementation or successful test does not make the proposal none. This is only a reporter-proposed approach, not maintainer approval or an observed fix. The translator alternative adds a third node and is not a resolved instance of the original two-node pair.

notes: Only one message definition is published. Different hashes do not justify an additional same-nominal-type definition_mismatch condition because the nominal types already differ and the Java definition is not supplied. The proposal's lidar_obstacle_detection/gdxboxesmessage spelling is preserved verbatim, not silently treated as the publisher's established type name.
